description: Asyncer, async and await, focused on developer experience.

summary.one_liner: Asyncer is a small Python library built on AnyIO that provides four utility functions for mixing async/await code with blocking code and concurrency, with an emphasis on editor autocompletion and type checking.
summary.what_it_does: Asyncer offers a small set of utility functions for working with async and sync code together. The README's sneak preview shows asyncify(), which wraps a blocking function so it runs in a worker thread without blocking the async event loop. The README says the library has just four functions, though only asyncify() is shown in detail. Asyncer is built on AnyIO, which is installed automatically as a dependency. The stated goal is better developer experience through autocompletion, inline editor errors, and mypy-friendly type checking. The README is a short description rather than a full API reference, and it points to a separate tutorial for each utility.
use_cases: call blocking sync function from async code
run blocking code in a worker thread
avoid blocking an asyncio or trio event loop
mix regular blocking code with async code
notable: Built on AnyIO, so it works with both asyncio and trio backends
Only four utility functions, keeping the surface small
Designed for editor autocompletion, inline errors, and mypy type checking
asyncify() runs sync functions in worker threads
caveats: The author describes it as very small and subjective, with changes possible in future versions
The README recommends pinning an exact version because the library may change
